A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRITLM study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite renumbering and pagination changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original GRITLM benchmark results, training ablations, KTO alignment experiments, and RAG performance and latency measurements in Sections 3–4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds RAG evaluations and retriever comparisons in Appendix D, Tables 10–11.

M1.justification: The joint objectives, bidirectional mean-pooled embeddings, causal generation, KTO alignment, and caching procedures are retained. Intermediate-layer embeddings and shared-sample training are suggestions, not implemented method changes.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds RAG evaluation on TriviaQA and MMLU. TriviaQA already appeared in v2's E5S training corpus, and MMLU already had generative evaluation; the added coverage concerns their RAG evaluation settings. Earlier coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v3 Table 11 adds BGE Large 0.34B, Base 0.11B, and Small 0.03B as NQ RAG retrievers with GRITLM 7B generating answers. BGE Large already appeared in standalone embedding comparisons, but these BGE retrievers were absent from v2's RAG comparison.

E3.justification: The added MMLU RAG experiment uses retrieval context and zero-shot Match scoring, alongside the retained main MMLU evaluation using exact match. Appendix D otherwise adopts Table 7's RAG setup; no revision to retained training or latency protocols is reported.

E4.justification: Appendix D newly reports a brief, unquantified manual inspection of BGE RAG samples, identifying irrelevant retrieved passages and confused generations. The existing attention, pooling, loss, precision, memory, and other ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Figure 5 retains standard deviations across 100 latency runs, and HumanEval retains its 20-sample generation procedure. The added RAG tables contain point estimates without new seed information, uncertainty estimation, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: New Table 10 reports RAG/doc-caching Match scores of 52.12/57.93 on TriviaQA and 51.10/53.46 on MMLU. New Table 11 reports NQ scores of 10.39, 10.31, and 10.17 for BGE Large, Base, and Small. Existing benchmark and ablation results are retained.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3 and the memory-saving decomposition in v2 Appendix G, now Appendix H, are unchanged. No new mathematical definition, derivation, theorem, or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and central unification claims remain unchanged. The introduction adds a pretraining-inclusive compute advantage and foregrounds existing refinements as novel. The conclusion newly claims around 10% better retrieval through reranking, although unchanged Table 3 shows only 57.4 to 57.9.

C2.justification: v3 expands discussion of pretraining costs, intermediate-layer embedding trade-offs, shared-sample training, and BGE retrieval failures. Appendix D also adds an unsubstantiated assertion that causal embedding attention guarantees performance equal to 'not using RAG'; no corresponding demonstration is provided.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 newly identifies binarized UltraFeedback as the dataset for the existing KTO experiments. Appendix Q adds 72 and 1760 H100 80GB GPU hours for the generative-only and embedding-only baselines, respectively. These are disclosures rather than established training changes.

R1.justification: The references add Cui et al.'s UltraFeedback and Joshi et al.'s TriviaQA. The introduction more explicitly positions existing training refinements as novel, while Section 6's related-work discussion and overall research positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized introduction and conclusion rewrites, expanded explanatory prose, and a new Additional RAG Results appendix. Section 4 corrects the latency figure reference and reversed Sample A/B references. Most narrative structure and wording are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 10–11, resizes or reformats Figures 1 and 3, and expands Figure 5's caption with already documented hardware information. Retained material is repaginated, including Table 6 and subsequent appendix tables, without a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Appendix D modestly strengthens caching validation beyond v2's Natural Questions experiment and adds smaller-retriever comparisons. Newly disclosed KTO data and baseline compute improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh localized new inaccuracies, although the unsupported 10% reranking claim and Appendix D's attention-equivalence assertion limit the improvement.
